column3: Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “conflict” as “opposition” and reorders the verse.
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “come from” and renders “trickery” as “deceit.”
NASB follows the critical text; “who is examining” is rendered “who examines.”
NASB renders “were we with a word of flattery” as “we never came with flattering speech” and sets “God is witness” off with dashes.
NASB includes “even though as apostles of Christ we might have asserted our authority,” which belongs to v. 7 in the Greek.
NASB reads “gentle,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “infants.” It begins after the clause moved to v. 6 and renders “cherish” as “tenderly cares for.”
NASB follows the critical text (“yearning”); it renders the phrase as “Having thus a fond affection for you” and “beloved” as “very dear.”
NASB follows the critical text without “for”; “remember” is rendered “recall,” and it adds “how.”
NASB adds “and so is God” and renders “holily and righteously” as “devoutly and uprightly.”
NASB moves “exhorting and encouraging and imploring,” which stand in v. 12 in the Greek, into this verse and adds “would.”
NASB begins after the participles moved to v. 11; “unto your walking” is rendered “so that you may walk.”
NASB follows the critical text (“And”); it renders the clause as “for what it really is” and “works” as “performs its work.”
NASB reorders the verse and renders “you suffered the same things” as “you also endured the same sufferings.”
NASB follows the critical text without “their own”; “opposed” is rendered “hostile,” and it begins a new sentence.
NASB follows the critical text (“wrath” without “of God”); it adds “the measure of.”
NASB renders “for the time of an hour” as “for a short while” and “in face, not in heart” as “in person, not in spirit.”
NASB follows the critical text (“For”); “once and twice” is rendered “more than once,” and “hindered” is “thwarted.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Christ”; “boasting” is rendered “exultation.”
Close to the Greek.
